metadata.creator: Żuchowski, Krzysztof

165.arb_toolchain_note: python-flint/libarb is not installed locally. The analytic cancellation theorem was executed, but a full Arb ball-FFT certificate was not claimed.
165.Dirichlet_tail_theorem: For decreasing a_d=d^(-eta), |sum_(d>D) a_d exp(i lambda d)| <= (D+1)^(-eta)/|sin(lambda/2)| away from resonance.
165.remaining_object: A formally rounded evaluation of the average polylogarithmic component and finite FFT cells in one ball-arithmetic engine.
165.status: Proven analytic tail theorem; formal full certificate open
165.confidence: Proven formula; strong numerical bound evaluation
165.claim_boundary: The cancellation result removes the oscillatory-tail bottleneck but is not presented as an Arb-certified full-window remainder.

166.classification_theorem: Under alpha_n=n alpha and h_n=h^n, alpha_n/h_n is not intensive. Every copy-invariant rule may depend on alpha/log(h), leaving an arbitrary function or normalization; composition alone does not select ln(2).
166.coarse_graining_test: Merging or splitting character sectors changes cardinality while leaving the carrier energy convention independently adjustable; the quotient by raw cardinality is not coarse-graining natural.
166.status: Refuted as tensor-intensive derivation; retained as one-copy axiom
166.claim_boundary: The result falsifies the cardinality formula under declared composition laws, not every possible future source theorem for beta.

168.algorithmic_modulus: delta(Q)=min_(1<=q<=Q)||q theta||. If q_n<=Q<q_(n+1), continued-fraction best-approximation theory computes the minimum from the convergent/semiconvergent data up to that breakpoint.
168.positivity_theorem: For each finite Q, delta(Q)>0 because theta is irrational and the minimum is over a finite set.
168.computability_theorem: Because pi is computable and theta is irrational, interval refinement decides every finite comparison and yields an algorithmic all-Q modulus when the continued fraction is generated.
168.practical_obstruction: The algorithmic stair modulus depends on all future partial quotients. It is an effective procedure, not a fixed kappa,nu power law suitable for a global Abelian remainder.
168.status: Proven algorithmic modulus; useful polynomial rate open
168.claim_boundary: The extra continued-fraction digits are illustrative and are not used as an all-scale Diophantine proof.

169.multiplicative_family: For positive-real dimension valuations with regularity, v(xy)=v(x)v(y) gives v(d)=d^a; normalization leaves a free a.
169.additivity_uniqueness_theorem: If v:N->R_+ satisfies v(m+n)=v(m)+v(n) and v(1)=1, then induction gives v(n)=n. Tensor multiplicativity follows, and the normalized centre state is the Hilbert trace.
169.status: Proven classification/no-go in declared valuation classes
169.claim_boundary: A different enriched categorical law could select another state, but it would be new structure beyond invariance and standard valuation.

170.interpretation: The Gibbs readout varies smoothly and is not singularly fine-tuned, but exact 9/5 is lost under generic gap, degeneracy, or beta changes.
170.status: Proven differential stability; Monte Carlo robustness quantified
170.confidence: Proven locally; strong numerical global evidence

171.incompleteness_theorem: If M were a complete convertibility monotone on all states, equal M would permit conversion in both directions. Monotonicity of A_rel would then force equal A_rel, contradicted by the two states.
171.claim_boundary: Program 155 remains valid on its orbit line. The new theorem shows that additional monotones are necessary off that line.

172.theorem: With probability at least 1-delta, simultaneous DKW quantile brackets at both independent times give T in [log(L2/U1),log(U2/L1)]/log(t2/t1).
172.status: Proven iid/pixel theorem; memory counterexample quantified
172.confidence: Proven for iid; strong evidence for challenge
172.claim_boundary: The DKW interval concerns the observed convolved distribution. It does not perform UV-unstable detector deconvolution.

173.model: log Q_target=a_T+(T+g)log t; log Q_control=a_C+(T_C+g)log t, with known T_C.
173.identifiability_theorem: Two distinct times for target and a known-exponent control give rank four and identify T and shared gain g. Without the control, the target exponent and gain occupy the same design column.
173.status: Proven minimal rank theorem; optimal finite allocation executed
173.claim_boundary: The theorem requires the apparatus gain to be shared between target and control and the control exponent to be independently known.

174.status: Frozen composite protocol executed on held-out synthetic records
174.claim_boundary: The classifier tests six declared generators. It is not proof of model completeness and does not identify FIN ontology.

175.intertwiner_theorem: A nonzero intertwiner between one-dimensional Z representations exists iff their generator eigenvalues are equal.
175.minimum_new_data: One infinite-order character (frequency difference) and one U(1) phase offset, plus provenance selecting both.
175.status: Proven categorical obstruction and exact target-coded cocycle
175.claim_boundary: The cocycle is a typed completion slot, not a derivation: its parameters are the strict-minus-legacy target differences.

177.observer_paradox_result: U_t evolves amplitudes, P_t evolves classical path probabilities, and the POVM instrument creates outcome probabilities. P_t is not identified with collapse.
177.status: Proven finite CP-instrument construction; conditional physics model
177.confidence: Proven mathematics; no external physical evidence
177.claim_boundary: The model demonstrates AFIS type completeness and interference bookkeeping. It is not a strict FIN prediction or experimental validation.

global_verdict.deepest_result: A_ME fails tensor intensivity under the natural additive/multiplicative composition law. The most durable progress is therefore operational: a shared-gain control restores exponent identifiability, DKW gives finite-sample iid intervals, and a typed CP instrument cleanly separates wave evolution, diffusion, environment, detector, and record.
